english.title: Unlawfully obtain communications data - Part 1 Investigatory Powers Act 2016
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a relevant person, knowingly or recklessly, and without lawful authority, obtained communications data **(..SPECIFY DATA..) from **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a

(A)_[telecommunications operator which is not wholly or mainly funded out of public funds]_
(B)_[postal operator]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section11 of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For offences committed before 14th October 2024 see H18711.
(ii) See section 11(2) for a definition of 'relevant person'.
(iii) As per section 11(3), this offence does not apply to a relevant person who shows that the person acted in the reasonable belief that the person had lawful authority to obtain the communications data.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see Schedule 1 to the Interpretation Act 1978 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
Time limit for prosecutions:
None
